page.metaDescription: Automated price monitoring across Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, and any other retailer. Set criteria in plain English, get alerts on drops, restocks, and changes.
page.h1: Price monitoring software for any website
page.subtitle: One dashboard tracking prices across every retailer you care about. Plain-English rules, multi-channel alerts, five-minute check intervals.
page.intro: Price monitoring is the practice of tracking product pricing across the web for changes — drops, increases, promotional activations, restocks. WebMonitor.fyi handles the polling, change detection, and alerting so you don't have to refresh tabs. The price monitoring tool works with any publicly accessible product page: Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, eBay, Costco, hotel booking sites, electronics retailers, fashion sites, and direct-from-brand stores. Used by shoppers waiting on a deal, resellers tracking competitor pricing, procurement teams managing supplier catalogs, and travel planners watching hotel and flight rates.

features.title: Works on any retailer page
features.body: Not limited to a curated list — any publicly accessible product URL works. Pre-built templates for major retailers; free-form support for direct-from-brand stores and niche sites.

features.title: Plain-English criteria
features.body: Write the rule in normal language: "alert me when this drops below $X" or "tell me when a member-only price activates". No regex, no XPath, no scripting.

features.title: Adjustable check frequency
features.body: Five-minute checks for limited-time deals and restock hunting. Hourly for everyday tracking. Daily for slow-moving items. Pick per monitor.

features.title: Multi-channel delivery
features.body: Email, SMS, webhook into Slack/Discord/your-tool-of-choice. Match the channel to the urgency.

features.title: Visual history
features.body: See each detected change with the before/after page state. Useful when a listing modifies the photo, title, or seller without changing the price.

features.title: Bulk monitor management
features.body: Dozens to hundreds of monitors from one account. Tag them, group them, batch-edit them.

steps.title: Add the product URL
steps.body: From the dashboard, click Add New Monitor and paste any product page link.

steps.title: Write the criterion
steps.body: Anything from "alert me on any change" to "notify me when this drops by 15% or more and is in stock for Prime shipping". The AI parses the natural-language criterion into a watch rule.

steps.title: Pick a frequency and a channel
steps.body: Five-minute intervals for limited-time deals; hourly or daily for general tracking. Email, SMS, or webhook.

steps.title: Get alerts when something changes
steps.body: The alert includes the old value, the new value, and a link back to the listing.

page.limits: Price monitoring is constrained by what a retailer renders publicly. Personalized prices that only show after login, A/B-tested pricing that varies by user cookie, and prices hidden behind a member portal are outside what a public-page monitor can see. For those, an authenticated integration is required, which the standard product doesn't cover.

faq.a: Reading publicly available web pages is legal under US law and most other jurisdictions. WebMonitor uses standard web requests at reasonable intervals, respects robots.txt as a baseline guideline, and does not bypass paywalls or login walls. Anti-scraping case law (HiQ v. LinkedIn, etc.) has generally found public-page scraping permissible. We do not, however, provide legal advice — for high-volume commercial monitoring, check with counsel.

Aggressive sub-minute polling triggers anti-bot defenses on most major sites. WebMonitor uses sane intervals (five minutes is the floor on most plans), rotated request patterns, and reasonable rate limits. The result: monitors run reliably on major retailers without getting blocked.

faq.q: What's the difference between price monitoring and price comparison?
faq.a: Price comparison shows you the current price across multiple sites at one point in time (e.g., Google Shopping). Price monitoring tracks changes over time and alerts you when conditions are met. The two complement each other — compare once you have an alert.

faq.q: How is this different from browser extensions like Honey or CamelCamelCamel?
faq.a: Browser extensions are limited to specific retailers (CamelCamelCamel = Amazon only) and rely on you visiting the page. WebMonitor checks any retailer in the background at the interval you set — no browser tab required, no curation by the extension vendor.
